# `Q-5-23` — Invalid `diagnostics:` entry

> An entry under `diagnostics:` was not in a recognized form. It has no
> effect: the diagnostic it names is still reported.

## What this means

The `diagnostics:` key maps an error code to what Quarto should do with
it. Each entry takes one of two forms:

```yaml
diagnostics:
  Q-2-49: off                    # short form

  Q-2-45:                        # long form, with a reason
    level: off
    reason: "legacy corpus, migrating incrementally"
```

`off` is the only level Quarto currently supports.

This warning fires when an entry does not match either form — a
misspelled level, a long-form entry with no `level:` key, or a
`diagnostics:` value that is not a map. Quarto reports it rather than
ignoring it because there is no schema layer to catch the mistake for
you: an entry that is silently dropped would look exactly like a
suppression that failed to work.

## How to fix

Check the entry against the two forms above. In particular:

```yaml
diagnostics:
  Q-2-49: error      # not supported — `off` is the only level
  Q-2-49:            # long form missing `level:`
    reason: "..."
  diagnostics:       # must be a map, not a list
    - Q-2-49
```

Writing a `reason:` is optional but worth the line — it is what makes
the suppression reviewable later, when whoever reads the file next has
to decide whether it still applies.

## Notes

Two limits are worth knowing when a suppression appears not to work:

- **Errors are never suppressed**, only warnings and informational
  diagnostics. Silencing an error would ship broken output with no
  signal at all.
- **Only diagnostics that carry a code can be suppressed.** Some Quarto
  warnings do not yet have one.
